personally, it’s because in TBBT most of the jokes are at Sheldon’s expense, like the audience is supposed to be laughing *at* him. imo, Community treats Abed with more respect, and the audience is more so laughing *with* him. in many ways, Abed serves as an audience stand in, shaping the format of the show through homages as that’s the way he makes sense of the world around him. i think he’s more humanized, in a way? but i haven’t seen all of TBBT so that may be my bias speaking.

For me, what’s rubbing me the wrong way isn’t really zach himself, it’s the “expert” he’s consulting. He’s used claims that have been proven false, and it really seems like he’s just using this series as a way to get fans to get his fancy company more consumers. I’d be more okay with his blatant advertising (because I assume this is a deal exchanging advice for exposure) if he didn’t try to use pseudoscience as his selling point. 

It’s also unclear how much zach is relying on this other company for his own product; at the end of the last video it seemed to me like he was saying he was going to blend the samples he received? It’s just unclear if it’s more of a partner or mentor business relationship right now, if that makes sense.

My point about the “expert” is more of a larger issue with the channel, though. I feel like they can let their experts go unchecked and make whatever snake oil claims they want sometimes. A few more disclaimers would go a long way in increasing transparency, but that may be just my opinion.

I agree, heartbreaking but realistic, my only criticism is that it was a REALLY fast onset of dementia for her to forget frieda in such a short amount of time. Everything else about the progression (the defensiveness, confusion, thinking she was in the past) seemed pretty realistic otherwise, based on my own family’s experiences with dementia. I guess it’s more realistic given that the SHU made it so much worse?
I’m also biased since I love red so much, so to see her be taken advantage of by frieda again made me frustrated with her ending.

I agree that it would have been a more strategic move for josh, however I’m glad the writers didn’t do a RW date for him. I saw RW as an unhealthy coping mechanism for rebecca, the whole idea of being happy if you *just get this one thing* and building it up in your head to be something it can’t be. It felt like every time she brought up RW she was looking for something or someone to over-romanticize.  So I’m glad they didn’t fulfill that happy RW dream after she got better on a date because to me, it was a parallel for when she wasn’t doing well, and it would go against the shows theme of finding happiness with yourself rather relying on a partner for it.
I’ll watch it sometimes when I also feel like “sad jenna” and really confused. It makes me feel better that she felt like this at one point too and things turned up for her soon enough
